# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. - **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). | run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
