Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. **Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.

Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

Hold on. The mock judge returns '[2]'. In the NEW 24-read scenario: entry [2] = the user turn ('count the words') → `entry.exempt` → `continue` → NOTHING hidden. The hide is a no-op in BOTH the old and new scenarios!

Hmm wait, but the PR claims the post-fold E1 basis is 12.9k measured. If the judge hide is a no-op, what freed the tokens? Maybe the structured engine has a deterministic fallback when the judge produces no effective hide — "the deterministic fallback" mentioned in judge.dart line comment: "The live-edge floor shared by every hide path (judge picks, the deterministic fallback, LRU re-hide, agent hide)". So when judge picks are no-ops, the engine falls back to a deterministic hide (hiding oldest hideable groups not in the protected tail, presumably). The deterministic fallback WOULD hide the reads group if the group doesn't touch the protected tail.

With the NEW shape: the group = {[3], [4]..[27]} — 25 records. Does the group touch the protected tail ([20]-[27])? YES — the results [20]-[27] are in the group. "a group touching the protected tail is dropped entirely (a hidden call with a live result orphans the wire)".

So with ONE carrier + 24 results in one group, the group ALWAYS touches the protected tail (the last 8 entries are results of that same group). The hide can NEVER free anything in this scenario — neither judge picks nor the deterministic fallback (which also respects the protected tail: "The live-edge floor shared by every hide path").

Then how did the measured run free tokens?? Unless... the engine, when hide paths fail, does a CHECKPOINT compaction (classic summarizer path) which replaces the whole pre-checkpoint span with a summary — that's the `<conversation>` summarizer path in the mock. The checkpoint fold (ckpt) replaces records [2..27] with a summary — checkpoints aren't bound by the protected tail in the same way?

Hmm wait. Let me reconsider. What does "the fold" in this test actually do? The test asserts '● auto-compacted' receipt. The auto-compactor: guard refuses → relief chain: structured passes (judge hides) → classic fall-through (checkpoint summarizer) → retry. The classic checkpoint fold replaces the entire history up to the checkpoint with a summary + protected tail? Or everything?

If the classic checkpoint fold replaces everything with a summary, then post-fold context = summary + system + new user turn → tiny → E1 basis 12.9k... hmm, 12.9k is big for a summary-based transcript. The summary would be the _foldCheckpoint text (~7 tokens). 12.9k implies most content survived. So the classic fold must keep the protected tail too (last 8 ledger records = last 8 read results ≈ 8 × 923 ≈ 7.4k + system + E1 turn + summary ≈ 12.9k — that fits! "the fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records)").

So the mechanics: judge picks no-op → deterministic fallback... also touches tail → no-op → classic checkpoint fold → keeps protected tail (8 lean results ≈ 7.4k) + summary → post-fold ≈ 12.9k with E1. And with the OLD shape: protected tail = 8 fat results ≈ 8 × 3k ≈ 24k > overflow line → E1 lands within ~1k of the guard line → jitter flips it. That's exactly the PR's story. ✓ The arithmetic checks out — 8 protected tail records is what matters, whether reads are fat or lean.

OK so the fix is sound. Now the mock judge comment: "The hide-judge: picks the oldest pairs (validation drops whatever is protected — a no-op hide is fine for the badge scenario)". In the new shape, is the hide still a no-op? Judge picks [2] = user turn → exempt → no-op. YES still a no-op — the judge's pick is the user turn which is exempt. The comment remains accurate ("a no-op hide is fine"). The badge comes from the classic checkpoint fold. OK so the mock comment is NOT stale. Good thing I checked.

Hmm, but wait — with 8 reads old shape: entries [2] user, [3] carrier, [4]-[11] results. Protected tail = last 8 = [4]-[11] = ALL results. Judge picks [2] → exempt → no-op. Same. So the judge was always a no-op; the fold comes from the classic path. The PR text says "the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (records: 0 hidden in every captured receipt)" — [2] is exempt OR its group touches tail; either way dropped. Consistent.

Now the deterministic fallback — would it fire and hide the group when judge picks are no-op? The group touches the protected tail in both shapes → dropped → no-op. Consistent.

So the ONLY fold that ever happens is the classic checkpoint summarizer path, and its floor is the protected tail. The fix reduces the tail weight. Sound.

Now — is there any chance the structured pass DOES hide with the new shape making E1 even smaller? Irrelevant — smaller is fine.

**Second-deep-check: does 24 lean reads still overflow the 16384 cap at the second request?** 24 × 3689 chars = 88,536 chars content → but tool results include line-number prefixes? Let me check the read tool output format in this repo. The read tool may add line numbers ("cat -n" style), inflating chars. Whatever — ≥22k > 16384. ✓ Overflow at the second request happens. ✓

But hmm — one more: the guard fires at the SECOND request. The second request = first turn + 24 tool results. Before the fold, the transcript is ~22k+ → guard refuses → relief chain → classic fold → retry succeeds with the continuation ('done: recovered', slow 2.5s). The badge paints during the slow continuation. ✓ scenario intact.

**E1 arithmetic:** post-fold transcript = system prompt + summary/checkpoint + protected tail (last 8 results ≈ 7.4k tokens) + continuation reply + user 'say hi'. ≈ 12.9k measured. Under 16384 by 3.4k. ✓ Headroom is comfortable vs any plausible jitter (path lengths, timestamps — tens of bytes, not thousands of tokens).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# pr-1597: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain

## Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +29
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:35Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

## Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

The key question for the review: does the new scenario still overflow the 16384 cap at the second request? 22k > 16384 → yes. ✓

And post-fold: with 24 reads, the protected tail = last 8 ledger entries. Post-fold, the E1 request ≈ system + first user turn + remaining results + summary. Claimed 12.9k measured vs 16384 → 3.4k headroom. Plausible, and the PR says it was measured headlessly.

  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain",
    "description": "## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598"

## Review Summary — PR #1597 (fix: nightly header_badge_pty razor edge)

**Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES** (1 blocking, 1 suggestion)

The PR's diagnosis of the Oct-11/12/13 reds is sound and its turn-1 scenario rework works (fold receipt, badge, `done: recovered`, badge-clear all pass locally). But the fix's central claim — *"E1 can never enter relief at all"* — compares the measured E1 basis (12898 tokens) against the wrong line. The over-window guard sits at 16384, but the **pre-flight auto-compactor triggers at `window − window~/4` = 16384 − 4096 = 12288** (`CompactionSettings.forWindow` → `shouldCompact`, `lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart:452,488`). E1's post-fold floor (~12.9k: protected 8-record tail + ~5.5k fixed overhead) is parked ~600 tokens **past** that trigger and cannot drop under it — so E1 enters the compaction chain deterministically, on every host.

**I reproduced it**: ran the changed PTY test on this linux CI-class runner (openpty works here, unlike the author's host) → `0 tests passed, 1 failed` at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:98` (the E1 `hi!` 90s wait), with the captured status row showing `ctx 80% (13.0k/16.4k) · 0tok · turn 3` and `Compacting context…` live mid-E1 — the exact mid-compaction-at-timeout face as the Oct-14 nightly red. The nightly on this branch would stay red. Fix direction (in the inline thread): shrink per-read size / grow count (e.g. ~30 × 60-line reads → turn-1 ≈ 18.5k > 16384, E1 floor ≈ 10.4k < 12288), plus a static guard pinning the shape to `hideProtectTailEntries` and the trigger arithmetic.
